name: Blesmolfolk Queen
body:
To every hive there is a Queen. A blesmolfolk Queen might rule over a thousand of her lesser kindred or a mere twelve, but, to her own hive, her position remains close to deific. The Queen is the hive’s mother, its ruler, and, on the almost-unheard-of occasion when true diplomacy is needed, its representative to other peoples.

No blesmolfolk queens are born as queens—they start out as warriors, before the death or departure of the previous Queen launches one lucky warrior into power. However, this process—usually run by the consorts—almost always selects a newborn warrior to undergo the biological shifts, and queens who have been raised as warriors are exceptionally rare.

Physical Description: Blesmolfolk queens are massive and bloated, standing nearly ten feet tall and weighing upwards of a thousand pounds. Their skin is pink and wrinkled, and they go unclad when possible. Unlike other blesmolfolk, a Queen’s eyes have no constant coloration, though red, black and green are most common. Queens share the massive, prehensile incisors that sets their species apart, and thanks to their slow metabolism, queens can live as long as 2,000 years. Like most blesmolfolk, queens move and speak with painstaking slowness. Many queens use staves and rods as symbols of office, which secretly double as walking sticks or canes; their immense bulk makes movement more difficult as they age. The vast majority of blesmolfolk queens are female, and all (even the males) are birthgiving. A Queen can give birth to massive litters (between 5 per year to 50 per month), but it depends on how well she is fed and how many consorts she has. Queens have some ability to subconsciously regulate litter size.

Society: Although the Queen’s technical duties are simple reproduction, and they are expected to allow the consorts to handle the actual ruling, it is rare that this suits either side. The Queen serves as the arbiter of blesmolfolk law, managing her hives to a microscopic level. Queens treat consorts as rather disposable, and watch warriors closely—some warriors are potential queens, and these ones are, in a best-case-scenario, kept under heavy surveillance at all times. Queens get along well with workers in the few times they interact, and it is out of respect for their Queen that blesmolfolk workers obey the whims of consorts and warriors.

This said, there is a darker side to the Queen’s role. Many queens, particularly of larger hives, are heavily restricted in their options, forbidden from ever leaving the hive—or even their bedchambers. When consorts seek to treat the Queen as a puppet, this political reversal frequently leads to the truly decadent societies, ridden by corruption and intrigue. Alternatively, it can result in outright civil war: Queen and workers against consorts, with the warrior caste either splitting amongst themselves or deciding the outcome with their favor.

Relations: Queens have virtually no interaction with other races, but those who leave their hives, or who are forced to deal diplomatically with outsiders, tend to get along equally well with lawfully-inclined races. They respect discipline and tradition above all else, and so a duergar, hobgoblin and dwarf inspire roughly equal regard from a blesmolfolk queen.

Elves and gnomes are regarded as very wild by the queens, who see them as little better than their flighty consorts, and halflings are expected to show or feign respect. Those that do are paid very little mind, but those that don’t are seen as insubordinate, a grave offense in a queen’s eyes. Humans are seen as a difficult quantity to calculate, and so most queens look for a simple motivation to ascribe all humans, such as “gold” or “land.” It makes things easier in their minds, particularly as they otherwise rarely receive the respect they “deserve.”

Alignment and Religion: Blesmolfolk queens have painfully rigid, traditionalist views. They always seek what is best for their hives, but see their methods as being utterly superior. Most blesmolfolk queens are lawful neutral, and the rest are usually lawful good—evil queens and nonlawful queens are equally rare. Blesmolfolk queens honor gods of order and nobility above all others. In contrast, the mindset of a queen who spent her early life as a warrior tends to closely match that of other warriors, leading to rather dysfunctional societies.

Adventurers: A blesmolfolk queen abroad has either been driven out by a rival queen or lost her hive to some calamity. They tend to struggle with this role reversal, and tend to embrace party roles that allow them to manage the battlefield. As such, most blesmolfolk queens who adventure are bards or summoners.

Core Traits (13 RP)
Ability Score Modifiers: Blesmolfolk queens are hardy, their minds akin to steel traps, and their personalities truly indomitable, but their size makes them even slower than other blesmolfolk. They gain +2 Charisma, +2 Constitution, +2 Intelligence, and –4 Dexterity. 3 RP
Size: Large. Blesmolfolk queens are Large creatures and take a –1 size penalty to their AC, a –1 size penalty on attack rolls, a +1 bonus on combat maneuver checks and to their CMD, and a –4 size penalty on Stealth checks. A blesmolfolk queen takes up a space that is 10 feet by 10 feet and has a reach of 5 feet. 7 RP
Speed: Blesmolfolk queens have a base speed of 15 feet. –2 RP
Languages: Blesmolfolk queens begin play speaking only Blesmol. Queens with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Common, Elven, Draconic, Dwarven, Goblin, and Undercommon.
Other Traits
Natural Armor: Blesmolfolk queens’ blubbery skin grants them a +3 natural armor bonus. 5 RP
Pain Immunity: Blesmolfolk queens do not feel pain and are immune to all pain-based effects. They cannot be knocked unconscious from nonlethal damage, though they can still begin to take lethal damage if their nonlethal damage is equal to their total maximum hit points. 3 RP
Stubborn: Blesmolfolk queens gain a +2 racial bonus on Will saving throws against compulsion and charm effects. In addition, if a queen fails such a save, it receives another save 1 round later to prematurely end the effect if the spell or spell-like ability has a duration greater than 1 round. This second save is made at the same DC as the first. If it has a similar ability from another source (such as a rogue’s slippery mind class feature), it can only use one of these abilities per round, but can try the other on the following round if the first reroll ability fails. 3 RP
Queen’s Speech: A blesmolfolk queen is difficult for any blesmolfolk to refuse, even those from another hive. Three times per day as a full-round action, it may address any single lower-ranking blesmolfolk within hearing with a single, sharp command. This functions as command, using the queen’s Hit Dice as the caster level and its Charisma as the defining ability. 1 RP
Hold Breath: Blesmolfolk queens can hold their breath for a number of rounds equal to four times their Constitution score before risking drowning or suffocating. 1 RP
Small Eyes: Blesmolfolk queens can only see clearly out to 30 feet. Beyond there, all subjects gain concealment. Blesmolfolk take a –4 penalty on sight-based Perception checks. –5 RP
Alternate Racial Traits

The following racial traits may be selected instead of existing queen traits.

Oracle: Some queens possess the rare gift of second sight, making them important seers for their hives. It is a strange sort of mutation, and it makes them much more vulnerable to physical sensation as a side effect. These rare monarchs are often singled out for terrible fates, and it is rumored that oracular queens are much more likely than most to be cast out and forced to live as adventurers. They can use augury once per day as a spell-like ability, at a caster level equal to the queen’s Hit Dice. Queens with this trait do not gain the pain immunity trait.
Soft-Spoken: Not all queens have the same powerful manners. These queens take a gentler approach, and gain a +2 racial bonus to Diplomacy checks. This trait replaces queen’s speech.
Strong Vision: Some queens develop extremely good eyesight as a consequence of doing absolutely nothing else all day but sit around, sleep, and peer mistrustfully at their counselors. They gain a +2 racial bonus on Sense Motive checks, and Sense Motive is always a class skill for them. Their base speed is reduced to 10 feet. These queens do not gain the Small Eyes trait.
Warrior Queen: Some queens were warriors for a significant portion of their lives before ascending to the throne, and they often retain something of the warrior mindset even after becoming queen. They gain the craftsfolk and self armed traits, as per the blesmolfolk warrior racial traits. They do not gain queen’s speech or stubborn.
